solution: TIGER has vowels I, E and consonants T, G, R. The even positions are 2 and 4; requiring the vowels to avoid them puts both vowels in the odd positions \(\{1,3,5\}\): \({}^3P_2=6\) ways. The 3 consonants fill the remaining 3 positions: \(3!=6\). Total \(=6\times6=36\). Matches option B.

X is \(3\times3\), Y is \(2\times3\), Z is \(3\times2\). I: \(ZY\) is \(3\times3\), so \((ZY)X\) is \(3\times3\) — defined, order 3 (true). II: \(XZ\) is \(3\times2\), so \(Y(XZ)\) is \(2\times2\) — defined, order 2 (true). III: \(YZ\) is \(2\times2\), so \(X(YZ)\) needs X's 3 columns to equal YZ's 2 rows — undefined (true). All three statements hold. Matches option D.

The circle \(x^2+y^2+gx+fy+\tfrac{c}{4}=0\) has centre \((-\tfrac{g}{2},-\tfrac{f}{2})\); touching the y-axis means it meets \(x=0\) at \((0,-\tfrac{f}{2})\). The normal at that point is the diameter through the centre, meeting the circle again at the antipodal point \(2\cdot(-\tfrac{g}{2},-\tfrac{f}{2})-(0,-\tfrac{f}{2})=(-g,-\tfrac{f}{2})\). Matches option B.

Statement 1: for \(x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta=p\) the distance from \((\alpha,\beta)\) is \(|\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta-p|\) (with \(-p\)); the printed \(+p\) is wrong, so statement 1 is false. Statement 2: the line \(\tfrac{x}{a}+\tfrac{y}{b}=1\) is \(bx+ay-ab=0\), whose distance is \(\left|\tfrac{b\alpha+a\beta-ab}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\right|\); the printed \(a\alpha+b\beta\) has the coefficients swapped, so statement 2 is false. Neither statement is correct. Matches option D.
With \(t=x-1\to0\), \(f(x)\to1\) (a \(1^\infty\) form). \(\ln L=\lim\dfrac{\ln f(x)}{g(x)}=\lim\dfrac{(a^t+b^t-2)/2}{t}=\dfrac{\ln(ab)}{2}\), so \(L=e^{\ln(ab)/2}=\sqrt{ab}\). Matches option A.
